**1\. Omni Flatforms**

*\- The problem:*

* Nowadays, individuals and small businesses commonly publish content on more than one social media platform in order to reach their audience wherever they are, most commonly on Facebook and LinkedIn. However, each platform has its own posting interface, login process, and formatting rules, which forces users to repeat the same upload process separately on each one.  
* Motivated by this problem, we propose to design and build a web-based platform that allows users to manage and distribute content to their Facebook and LinkedIn accounts from a single, unified interface

*\- Targeted users:*

The platform is intended for two main types of end users:

* Individual content creators, who manage their own social media presence alone  
* Small-to-medium businesses, where multiple staff members are involved in producing and publishing content. 

To support both cases, the system provides two account roles. A manager account is used by a business owner or social media lead; it can add members (their inferiors) to a specific workspace, and is responsible for reviewing draft content submitted by members and deciding whether it can be published.  The member account, can compose content and submit it for the manager's review and, hence, they cannot publish their post directly. 

An individual user (a content creator working alone) has the same content-creation abilities as a content creator, but is not subordinate to any manager \- when working alone, the individual user reviews and publishes their own content directly, without needing approval from anyone else.

*\- Our USP (unique selling point):*

* AI content generation grounded in reference sources/saved prompts (NotebookLM-style)  
* AI-generated performance reports from interaction stats \- competitors have analytics dashboards, but framing it as an AI-generated narrative report (not just charts) is a differentiator worth calling out explicitly  
* Multi-platform distribution

Among the other competitors (Buffer, Hootsuite, Metricool, SocialPilot, Loomly, etc.), none of them provide our first feature. Their AI features are generic caption writers or repurposing tools \- not source-grounded generation like our approach.

* **Project Management Methodology (Agile / Scrum Framework):**
  * **Development Framework:** 2-week Sprint cycles following the Agile/Scrum framework with clear sprint goals and deliverables.
  * **Sprint 1 (Weeks 1–2):** Requirement Specification & Project Skeleton (SRS PA01, Figma wireframes, Base React + FastAPI setup).
  * **Sprint 2 (Weeks 3–4):** Architecture Design & Core Prototype (Database Schema EERD PA02, Auth JWT, Workspace & PIN join).
  * **Sprint 3 (Weeks 5–6):** Feature Scaling & Testing (AI Content Generation, Task Management, Distribution, Manual Test Cases PA03).
  * **Sprint 4 (Weeks 7–8):** Integration, Test Automation, Packaging & Final Review (n8n workflows, Integration test suites, Final Demo & Slides PA04).
  * **Collaboration Tools:** GitHub (Git Flow branching strategy), Discord (Weekly sync & daily standups), Figma (UI Mockups), Swagger UI / Postman (API testing).
